subject: Third-party vendor addition — 60-day notice, eSign sequencing & data transfer selection
participants_external: maria.gonzalez@acme-cloud.com (Maria Gonzalez, Legal Counsel, Acme Cloud Services)
messages:
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: maria.gonzalez@acme-cloud.com, procurement@acme-cloud.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: onboarding Acme Cloud Services vendor (60-day review) + signature path

Hi Maria / Acme team,

Quick heads-up: Procurement has approved a trial integration with Acme Cloud Services for our telemetry ingestion pipeline. Per our DPA and privacy practice, we need to notify internal stakeholders and give a 60-day review window before the vendor is formally added to production.

What we need from you this week:
- DocuSign envelope with the DPA redline accepted or a clear set of redline positions we can route (we prefer DocuSign for execution).
- SCCs / EU transfer mechanism confirmation and a short data flow diagram (where customer data is stored/processed).
- Evidence for controls: SOC2 Type II report and encryption-at-rest screenshots or high-level ATO statements.

We plan to:
- Start the 60-day quiet period on receipt of the signed envelope or confirmation of SCCs in place.
- Use a staggered signature sequence: Acme signs first, then Redwood legal, then procurement sign-off (see attached proposed sequence).
- Allow a 7-day emergency early activation only where a security-critical fix is required and the security team signs off.

Cc'ing Rishi (procurement) and Neha (privacy) to confirm internal sequencing and objection evaluation criteria.

Thanks — please push the DocuSign link when ready.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Contracts & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed-DocuSign-Sequence.pdf
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, maria.gonzalez@acme-cloud.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: onboarding Acme Cloud Services vendor (60-day review) + signature path

Thanks, Olga — a few privacy items to clarify before we start the formal clock: 

1) Transfer mechanism: we need explicit confirmation which mechanism Acme intends to rely on for EU -> US transfers. Options we accept:
   - Updated EEA Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) executed between parties (preferred), OR
   - Adequacy + contractual appendix explaining processing boundary, OR
   - Supplementary technical measures (pseudonymization + limited key access) plus SCCs.

2) Scope of data: please include a concise table in the diagram indicating categories of personal data and whether it will be persisted or only transient in memory.

3) Objection grounds: for clarity in the 60-day review, we'll evaluate on: data type sensitivity, geographic residency requirements, encryption strength, vendor SOC2 gaps. We'll escalate to CISO if any high-impact gaps are identified.

If Acme can provide the SCCs PDF + SOC2 report and confirm they will accept Redwood's minimal redlines (we only require a 30-day notice for subcontractor changes, and a 7-day emergency exception), we can proceed to routing the DocuSign envelope.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Hi Olga / Neha — thanks for the clarity. We can do the following: 

- Attached: Acme-SCCs-and-Data-Flow-Diagram.pdf and SOC2-TypeII-Report-2026.pdf (redacted sections removed as standard).
- We are prepared to execute the updated EEA SCCs as the primary transfer mechanism.
- For supplementary controls, we confirm AES-256 at-rest encryption; keys are managed by our KMS with role-based access. We will provide screenshots for verification.

DocuSign: we prepared a single envelope with the DPA (our standard redline accepts SCCs but proposes a 45-day objection window instead of 60). We can accept a staggered signing order — Acme -> Redwood Legal -> Redwood Procurement — but Acme will need to sign first to bind our internal provisioning team.

Regarding emergency early activation: we prefer written procurement approval plus a security checklist signed by vendor-security@acme-cloud.com. We can support a 7-day early activation with those two approvals.

Link to envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the sequence.

Best,
Maria Gonzalez
Legal Counsel, Acme Cloud Services

Attachments: Acme-SCCs-and-Data-Flow-Diagram.pdf, SOC2-TypeII-Report-2026.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, maria.gonzalez@acme-cloud.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: onboarding Acme Cloud Services vendor (60-day review) + signature path

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Maria. A couple of procurement notes and a proposed objection matrix to keep things consistent across vendors: 

- Procurement accepts Acme's preference for a 45-day objection window only if privacy signs off; otherwise we'll default to the 60-day window. So Neha, can you confirm by EOD Monday whether the 45-day variant is acceptable conditional on the SCCs + SOC2 report?

- DocuSign sequencing: fine with Acme signing first. Please ensure the envelope includes an explicit field for the provisioning handoff date (provisioning will not start until the full acceptance block is signed by Redwood). Our suggested sequence in the attached PDF is: Acme legal -> Redwood Legal -> Redwood Procurement -> Provisioning acknowledgement.

- Objection matrix (high level):
   * Block: unresolved critical controls gap (ex: encryption not at-rest, data residency violation) -> hold onboarding, escalate to CISO.
   * Mitigate: medium gaps (SOC2 findings that are scheduled remediation) -> conditional onboarding with compensating controls & 30-day remediation plan.
   * Accept: minor administrative differences (eg: notice window lower than 60d but documented) -> allow with procurement acceptance.

If Neha can confirm SCCs+SOC2 are sufficient, I will route the envelope for signatures on Monday.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Procurement
Redwood Inference
